answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to post a bond that is slashed if its actions are proven fraudulent. A single attacker may create thousands of accounts, but each must lock real capital, and coordinated abuse risks losing the entire stake; identities are cheap, while the bond is not. For example, a juniper-market agent could earn trust through verified trades, with each ripple of suspicious referrals triggering review before rewards are released at dawn. This raises the cost of a Sybil attack without pretending to make fake identities impossible.
